input_signals.name: Solvency_Scored_BookToMarket
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(re, at), RATIO(wcap, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheapness earns a premium only when the balance sheet shows accumulated earnings capacity and working-capital slack; cheap firms with depleted retained earnings and negative working capital are distressed traps whose low price reflects default risk rather than mispricing.
input_signals.reasoning: Retained-earnings-to-assets and working-capital-to-assets are the two classic Altman channels that separate solvent from failing firms, and combining their ranks with the book-to-market rank isolates cheap-and-solvent firms in the top of the composite. The composite deliberately down-weights high book-to-market firms that are cheap because of cumulative losses and liquidity strain, which is the trap side of the value spread.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), sumrank( ratio( re, at ), ratio( wcap, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cheapness_Per_NetLiability_Burden
input_signals.expression: RATIO(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), ADD(1, RATIO(SUB(lt, che), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Observed book-to-market must be deflated by the net-liability burden the equity claim sits behind; a given level of cheapness is worth far less when net liabilities are a large fraction of assets because the equity is a levered residual option on a distressed asset base.
input_signals.reasoning: The denominator converts raw cheapness into cheapness per unit of net (cash-adjusted) liability intensity, so unlevered cheap firms rank far above equally cheap but heavily indebted firms. Netting cash against liabilities captures the fact that liquid reserves offset nominal leverage in default risk, making this more than a leverage-only or value-only sort.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), add( 1, ratio( sub( lt, che ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: SalesYield_Minus_LossPersistence
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(revt, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(pi), 0), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sales-to-price identifies operationally large but low-priced firms; whether such cheapness is a recovery option or a distress trap depends on whether losses are one-off or chronic, and chronic pretax losses signal a persistent, non-mean-reverting distress state.
input_signals.reasoning: Counting loss years over five fiscal years measures the persistence rather than the level of distress, which is precisely what separates temporarily depressed cyclical value from structurally impaired firms. Sales-to-price is the valuation anchor least contaminated by transitory earnings, so pairing it with loss persistence isolates the healthy-cheap corner.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( revt, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), neg( ts_sum( indicator( neg( pi ), 0 ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Conjunctive_Cheap_And_Liquid
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(act, lct), RATIO(re, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Compensated cheapness requires cheapness AND survivability simultaneously, not on average; a conjunctive (minimum) rule demands both conditions, so the long leg contains only firms that are cheap on EBITDA yield and liquid and solvent.
input_signals.reasoning: MIN implements an economic AND rather than the additive averaging of gen-0's SUMRANK, which allowed extreme cheapness to compensate for extreme distress and thereby filled the long leg with traps. The current-ratio and retained-earnings channels capture short-term liquidity and long-run accumulated solvency, the two distinct legs of bankruptcy risk.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( sumrank( ratio( act, lct ), ratio( re, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ClaimAdjusted_EBITDA_EV_Yield
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), lt)), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: True cheapness must be measured against every claim on operating cash flow, so operating profit relative to enterprise value (market cap plus liabilities minus cash) separates firms that are genuinely cheap from firms whose low equity price merely reflects a large liability stack sitting ahead of shareholders.
input_signals.reasoning: Equity-only value metrics label heavily indebted firms as cheap even when the whole enterprise is expensive, which is precisely the trap that gen-0 composites failed to exclude; embedding liabilities and cash in the denominator makes the distress structure part of the valuation ratio itself. Because HML is built from book-to-market, an EBITDA/EV yield is not mechanically spanned by it, giving a realistic chance of FF5 alpha alongside a monotone cross-sectional slope.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( ebitda, add( sub( mul( prcc_f, csho ), che ), lt ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: CashYield_With_Liquidity_Buffer
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheapness measured in realized operating cash flow, combined with a working-capital buffer large relative to total claims, identifies firms whose low price is not a solvency verdict; cash-flow-cheap firms with no buffer are the traps.
input_signals.reasoning: Cash-flow-to-price is much less collinear with HML than book-to-market, so the value half of this composite should not be fully absorbed by FF5, addressing the zero-alpha problem of Solvency_Scored_BookToMarket. The distress half uses net working capital scaled by total liabilities, which measures the runway to meet claims rather than another profitability level already captured by RMW.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) )

input_signals.name: Cheap_With_Improving_Solvency
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(DELTA(RATIO(pi, at), 1), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(lt, act), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among cheap firms the market underreacts to fundamental inflections: rising pretax profitability together with a falling ratio of total liabilities to current assets signals that distress risk is receding and the discount is about to be re-rated.
input_signals.reasoning: Levels of solvency and profitability are spanned by HML, RMW and CMA, which is why the gen-0 level composites had no alpha, whereas one-year changes in those quantities are largely orthogonal to factor loadings and are the documented source of Piotroski-style abnormal returns within value. Pairing book-to-market with a two-channel improvement score keeps the strong value-driven FMB slope while sourcing alpha from the change component.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), sumrank( delta( ratio( pi, at ), 1 ), neg( delta( ratio( lt, act ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: EbitdaYield_Liability_Runway
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheapness in operating-profit terms is compensated only when net working capital provides a runway large relative to all outstanding claims; the same yield with no runway is a firm being priced for liquidation.
input_signals.reasoning: This keeps the exact economic structure of the only archive signal with an aligned slope, alpha and Sharpe, but replaces the coverage-limiting oancf with ebitda, which is reported for a much longer and broader panel, so we learn whether the +4.9% alpha survives a near-doubling of coverage. Normalizing the buffer by total liabilities rather than assets is retained deliberately, since that is what makes the distress channel a solvency-runway measure rather than another asset-scaled profitability level already priced by RMW.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) )

input_signals.name: CashYield_Runway_Extended
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: The relevant valuation input is cash actually generated by operations relative to price, and when the cash-flow statement is unavailable operating profit is the economically correct fallback measure of the same quantity, so the healthy-cheap versus trap-cheap distinction should hold on the extended sample.
input_signals.reasoning: The COALESCE is economically justified rather than a coverage patch: both arguments measure the same cash-generation-to-price concept, with the accrual-free version preferred when reported. Paired with Signal 1, this isolates whether the alpha requires realized operating cash flow specifically or merely a cash-based yield, while restoring the coverage lost to post-1988 cash-flow reporting.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( coalesce( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) )

input_signals.name: Rollover_Risk_Adjusted_SalesYield
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(revt, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), lct))
input_signals.hypothesis: Distress is triggered by refinancing, not by leverage per se; a cheap firm holding cash in excess of the debt maturing within a year can survive to realize its value, whereas an equally cheap firm whose short-term debt exceeds its cash is one credit market closure from restructuring.
input_signals.reasoning: No archive signal has used the maturity structure of debt, yet the timing of claims is what converts weak fundamentals into actual default, and cash net of current debt scaled by current liabilities is the sharpest available proxy for that pressure. Sales-to-price is chosen as the value channel because it is the least sensitive to the depressed transitory earnings typical of firms under refinancing stress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( revt, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( sub( che, dlc ), lct ) )

input_signals.name: CashYield_Runway_Plus_RetainedBuffer
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt), RATIO(re, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Solvency has a flow-liquidity leg and a stock-of-past-earnings leg; a cheap firm is a compensated value opportunity only if it has both a working-capital runway and accumulated retained earnings relative to its claims, since retained earnings measure the cumulative equity cushion that liquidity alone cannot reveal.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's best signal uses only the working-capital runway, and retained-earnings-to-claims is the one solvency dimension that repeatedly carried predictive weight in gen-0 composites without duplicating current liquidity. Adding it as a nested channel tests whether the distress side of the interaction is under-specified rather than over-specified, at unchanged coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( coalesce( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), sumrank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ), ratio( re, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: SmoothedCashYield_Runway
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(MA(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 3), RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: A single year of operating cash flow scaled by price is noisy for exactly the firms at issue, since distressed firms swing between negative and windfall cash years; a three-year average identifies durable cash-generating capacity, so the healthy-cheap classification should be more stable and the trap side more cleanly separated.
input_signals.reasoning: This isolates one design choice — measurement horizon of the valuation channel — while holding the winning distress channel fixed, so the comparison against CashYield_Runway_Extended is interpretable. If smoothing raises both the alpha t-stat and Sharpe, the portfolio's turnover and composition instability were costing signal, which is a diagnosis we can then apply to the whole family.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ma( coalesce( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 3 ), ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) )

input_signals.name: Conjunctive_CashYield_Runway
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheapness and solvency must hold jointly rather than on average, so a multiplicative rank interaction should concentrate the long leg on firms that are simultaneously cash-cheap and claim-solvent and the short leg on firms failing both, sharpening the trap-versus-value spread.
input_signals.reasoning: SUMRANK lets extreme cheapness compensate for extreme illiquidity, which is precisely the trap the theme warns about, whereas the rank product penalizes any firm weak on either dimension without generating the mass-at-zero degeneracy that ruined the gen-1 INDICATOR gates. Comparing it to Signal 1 and to the archive additive version tells us whether the interaction is genuinely multiplicative.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( coalesce( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: CashYield_With_Claims_Turnover
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RATIO(revt, lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm that generates a large volume of revenue relative to its outstanding claims retains operating and refinancing options that a low-turnover firm with the same balance sheet does not, so revenue productivity of claims is a distinct survival dimension from static liquidity.
input_signals.reasoning: Revenue-to-claims is the Altman turnover channel expressed against liabilities rather than assets, and it has never been tested in this archive; it should be nearly uncorrelated with the working-capital runway while capturing the same cheap-and-viable versus cheap-and-shrinking distinction. Both inputs are broadly reported, so coverage should match the best of the family rather than the 0.08–0.09 of the oancf-only constructions.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( coalesce( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ratio( revt, lt ) )

input_signals.name: CashYield_WorstCase_Solvency
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: What separates a resilient cheap firm from a lottery-like one is not today's liquidity but the worst liquidity it has run in recent memory; a firm that never dipped into a negative claim-adjusted buffer over five years has demonstrated capacity to survive its own downside.
input_signals.reasoning: Current-level solvency can be window-dressed or temporarily flattered by asset sales, whereas the five-year minimum is a demonstrated-resilience statistic and is a genuinely different temporal concept from the levels, changes and trends already tested. If it improves on the current-level version, the trap-versus-value distinction is about tail survivability, which would then guide the final consolidation generations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( coalesce( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ts_min( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: Conjunctive_CashYield_WorstRunway
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A cheap firm is compensated value only if it has never lacked a claim-adjusted liquidity buffer in recent memory, so cheapness should be multiplied by demonstrated worst-case solvency rather than by a possibly window-dressed current snapshot.
input_signals.reasoning: This crosses the archive's two strongest ingredients — the multiplicative rank structure that lifted alpha to +6.0% and the five-year minimum runway that gave the strongest FMB slope — so it directly tests whether their contributions are additive in evidence. The worst-case statistic also stabilizes portfolio composition, which should raise Sharpe relative to the current-level conjunctive version.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( coalesce( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ) ), rank( ts_min( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Triple_Conjunctive_Cheap_Solvent_Productive
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)), RANK(RATIO(revt, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Survival requires both a liquidity stock and an operating flow large relative to claims, so a firm that is cash-cheap, liquid against its liabilities, and generating substantial revenue per unit of liabilities is the cleanest possible healthy-cheap firm, while failure on any one leg marks a trap.
input_signals.reasoning: Claims turnover delivered the archive's highest Sharpe (0.610) at full coverage, and the conjunctive structure delivered the highest alpha, so combining the two as a strict three-way conjunction should preserve alpha while improving spread quality. Unlike the failed additive enrichment with retained earnings, multiplication cannot let a strong leg mask a fatal weakness on another.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( coalesce( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ) ), mul( rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) ), rank( ratio( revt, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: StrictMin_CashYield_Runway
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The binding constraint on a cheap firm's return is its weakest dimension, so the return-relevant score is the minimum of cheapness and claim-adjusted liquidity rather than their product.
input_signals.reasoning: The product and the minimum encode different economics — the product still rewards an extreme on one axis while the minimum is governed purely by the bottleneck — and separating them is the cleanest way to learn what the multiplicative gain in gen 4 actually came from. This is deliberately a single-axis design test against Conjunctive_CashYield_Runway, holding both channels fixed.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( coalesce( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Conjunctive_SmoothedYield_Runway
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 3)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable cash-generating capacity, measured over three years, is the valuation input that should be interacted with solvency, because a one-year cash windfall or shortfall misclassifies precisely the distressed firms whose cash flows are most erratic.
input_signals.reasoning: Smoothing improved the FMB slope in the additive family while leaving alpha essentially unchanged, so testing it inside the superior multiplicative structure tells us whether horizon and structure improvements compound. It should also reduce month-to-month rebalancing of the long leg, a Sharpe-relevant diagnostic.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( coalesce( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 3 ) ), rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Conjunctive_CashYield_LowAccrualBuild
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms approaching distress conceal deterioration by building working capital — stuffing receivables and inventory — so a cheap firm whose working capital is expanding relative to its claims is a trap, while a cheap firm shrinking working-capital investment is converting operations into cash.
input_signals.reasoning: This introduces an earnings-quality distress channel that is a flow-of-accruals concept rather than another solvency level, so it is unlikely to be spanned by RMW or CMA and should add alpha where levels were absorbed. Scaling the working-capital change by total liabilities keeps the claim-relative normalization that has been the consistent discriminator in this archive, and using wcap rather than the oancf-minus-earnings accrual definition preserves full coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( coalesce( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( delta( wcap, 1 ), lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Conjunctive_CashYield_FlowAndStock_Solvency
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(pi, lt), RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Solvency has a flow leg — pretax profit available to service claims — and a stock leg — liquid assets net of current obligations relative to claims — and a cheap firm needs both, since profitable firms can still fail on liquidity and liquid firms can still erode their cushion through losses.
input_signals.reasoning: Enriching the distress side additively hurt when the added channel was retained earnings, a slow-moving stock variable largely redundant with book equity, whereas pretax-income coverage of claims is a current flow measure that is economically complementary to the liquidity stock. Placing the enriched solvency score inside the multiplicative structure tests whether the earlier degradation came from the added channel itself or from additive dilution of the interaction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( coalesce( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ) ), rank( sumrank( ratio( pi, lt ), ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Conjunctive_SmoothedYield_WorstRunway
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 3)), RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Compensated cheapness requires durable cash generation, not a single year's figure, interacted with a liquidity cushion the firm has never lost; combining a three-year average yield with a five-year minimum claim-adjusted buffer should identify healthy-cheap firms with the least measurement noise on either axis.
input_signals.reasoning: Smoothing the valuation channel gave the archive's most reliable alpha (t = 4.02) and the minimum-runway distress channel gave its strongest slope (t = 6.15), and the two refinements act on different arguments of the product, so their gains plausibly compound rather than overlap. Both refinements also reduce turnover in the extreme deciles, which is where Sharpe has been improving through this family.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( coalesce( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 3 ) ), rank( ts_min( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Conjunctive_CashYield_Worst3yrRunway
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Resilience should be measured over the recent credit cycle rather than deep history, since a liquidity crunch five years ago may reflect a company that no longer exists in economic terms, while a crunch in the last three years is live information about fragility.
input_signals.reasoning: This isolates a single design parameter — the resilience window — against the current leader, and a shorter window also loses fewer young firms, so it distinguishes whether the gen-5 improvement came from downside conditioning or from implicitly requiring a long reporting history. If the three-year version matches the five-year version at higher coverage, the effect is genuinely about downside solvency rather than firm-age selection.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( coalesce( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ) ), rank( ts_min( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Conjunctive_WorstYield_WorstRunway
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TS_MIN(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 3)), RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm that looks cheap even on its worst recent cash-flow year, and that never ran out of a claim-adjusted buffer, is the purest form of compensated value, whereas a firm that is only cheap on a peak cash year is a cyclical trap dressed as value.
input_signals.reasoning: All previous valuation channels used current or averaged cash flow, so the downside of the cash-flow distribution has never been tested even though it is exactly what a distressed-equity valuation should be based on. Applying the same worst-case logic to both legs makes the signal a joint tail-survivability score, a substantively different economic statement from the mean-based versions.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ts_min( coalesce( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 3 ) ), rank( ts_min( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Conjunctive_CashYield_IndustryNormedRunway
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The liquidity buffer that constitutes safety is industry-specific — a level that is comfortable for a utility with predictable cash flows is dangerous for a retailer with inventory risk — so solvency should be judged against industry peers while cheapness is judged market-wide.
input_signals.reasoning: Every version so far ranks the buffer across the whole market, which mechanically loads the short leg with entire capital-intensive industries rather than genuinely fragile firms, an instability in portfolio composition that could be capping the alpha. Industry-ranking only the distress leg keeps the market-wide valuation sort intact and directly tests whether the trap identification is firm-specific or sectoral.
input_signals.author: proposer

input_signals.name: Conjunctive_CashYield_TotalClaimCoverage
